notes: DOCUMENTED TARGET - NOT RECORDABLE (daemon_capability: incapable). This spec states the arc the row asserts so a future re-assessment has something concrete to compare against; it is NOT expected to pass on hermes as it stands, and it is deliberately not weakened to match what hermes can do. THE ROW: a blocking dialog that belongs to NO tool call - ready -> working -> waiting entered while the modal is on screen with nothing in flight to carry the entry, waiting -> working -> ready once the user answers with nothing completing to carry the release, and a final ready that survives a >=15s trailing idle. AGENT LAYER (satisfied): hermes 0.19.0 raises three tool-less blocking modals from the CLI itself, each a _prompt_text_input_modal overlay (cli.py:8120) with no tool call and no LLM call - _confirm_destructive_slash (cli.py:10838) for /clear, /new, /reset and /undo, default ON via approvals.destructive_slash_confirm (hermes_cli/config.py:2774); _confirm_and_reload_mcp for /reload-mcp; and _confirm_expensive_model_switch (cli.py:8382) before a costly /model switch. A fourth tool-less dialog, the shell-hook first-use trust prompt (agent/shell_hooks.py:736-757), blocks before any session row exists. The row's sandbox/network trigger is absent (empty scan of tools/environments/); its MCP-elicitation trigger is present (tools/mcp_tool.py ElicitationHandler) but fires mid-tool-call, so the row excludes it. TRANSPORT LAYER (why this cannot pass): the adapter has two sensors and neither carries the entry edge. (1) The store: Source is ProcessOwnedStore over the shared $HERMES_HOME/state.db and watcher.go emits EventActivity only when sessions.message_count GROWS (watcher.go:44, 282, 416). A CLI modal writes no message row, so the watcher emits nothing at all and the session never even reaches `working` - the row's FIRST assertion, not just its waiting leg, is unproducible. (2) The hook channel, which is new on this column since 2.19 was assessed: this adapter installs pre_approval_request, post_approval_response and on_session_end (hookinstaller.go:232-236). hermes' _fire_approval_hook has exactly six call sites (approval.py:154, 162, 3099, 3167, 3576, 3592), all on dangerous-command approval paths; none of the modals is on any of them, and the CLI MCP-elicitation path bypasses the pair too (request_elicitation_consent calls prompt_dangerous_approval directly at approval.py:3933). Of hermes' 23 VALID_HOOKS (hermes_cli/plugins.py:135) the only one firing near this class is on_session_reset (cli.py:7491), which fires AFTER the user answers - a release-side-only signal, and one this adapter does not install. THE PHASES BELOW ASSERT THE ARC ANYWAY, unweakened, so that if an upstream event ever fires when a non-approval modal opens, this file is the target to verify against. ANCHORING follows this column's ProcessOwnedStore shape: the sessions row is INSERTed only on the first user message, so session_birth is anchored to recording start and left UNPINNED (the ready birth in a recording is the transient proc-<PID> pre-session), and every later phase chains through same_session_as: turn_start. The recipe would open a real turn first (a plain prompt) precisely so that a store-backed session exists for the modal's arc to attach to. LOAD-BEARING PRECONDITION, not an assumption: both slash modals are self-disabling - answering 'Always Approve' persists approvals.destructive_slash_confirm: false (cli.py:10915) permanently. On a host where that was ever answered, the slash command runs straight through, no modal opens, the session never leaves ready, and a weaker spec would go green having tested nothing. Any recording must re-probe the config value and answer 'once'. NO observations block: of verify hard-asserts only against the newest recording's replay-golden summary (internal/validate/observations.go:141-160), hermes' Parser sets only ev.ModelName (parser.go:78), and the store-derived token lift is gated to antigravity (cmd/replay/metrics.go:59) - so tokens_nonzero and cost_nonzero could never pass on this column, and a model pin on a cell that is never recorded would be a doc-guess.
source: .specs/agent-scenarios.md -> Feature: Blocking dialog without a tool call

text: A hermes session appears in ready shortly after the `hermes chat` REPL launches (expected to be the transient proc-<PID> pre-session - the store row does not exist until the first user message)
A PID is bound to the session (hermes is a Python console script, matched on the full command line)
A real turn opens the store-backed session ready -> working, so there is a session for the dialog's arc to attach to

The tool-less modal opens (on hermes: _confirm_destructive_slash / _confirm_and_reload_mcp / _confirm_expensive_model_switch, a prompt_toolkit overlay raised by the CLI with no tool call and no LLM call in flight) and the session goes working -> waiting. The entry edge is carried by nothing: no tool call opened, and none will complete to end it. Up to 15s is allowed because some agents publish this signal on a timer
The user answers the modal ('Approve Once', never 'always' - see the meta note) and the session resumes waiting -> working. The release edge is likewise carried by nothing: no tool result closes it
The turn finishes back to ready - full arc ready -> working -> waiting -> working -> ready

THE LOAD-BEARING PHASE. The session is still ready after a >=15s trailing idle: it does not fall back to waiting, and it was not left pinned at waiting from the dialog onward by something no later event retires
